messages:
Alex: Hey — quick question. Trying to add my spouse as a benefits dependent but they live in the UK and don’t have a US SSN. What proof do you need for enrollment? Any payroll/tax implications I should know about?

Maya: Congrats! :tada: You can generally add a spouse as a qualifying life event if the marriage was recent — typically you have 30 days from the event to enroll midyear. If you miss that window you can add them during open enrollment.

Maya: For documentation, carriers differ but we usually accept: passport + marriage certificate (certified English translation if original not in English). If there’s no SSN, an ITIN (or a pending W-7 application) is commonly accepted. Can you share when the marriage took place?

Alex: Married last month (Feb 10). Ok I’ll gather docs. Does the spouse need a US mailing address? They’re based in London and will stay there.

HR Bot: Automated reminder: enrollments for qualifying life events must be submitted within 30 days of the event to be processed mid-year. Submit docs in People Ops > Benefits > "Request Dependent Addition". Portal link: https://benefits.redwood.example/submit (internal only).

Liam: Note on coverage: most medical plans in our network are US-based providers — emergency coverage abroad varies by carrier and plan. If you expect regular UK care, the carrier may not reimburse routine services outside the US. Worth confirming with the carrier before relying on network benefits.

Carlos: FYI from carrier side: different carriers have different verification rules. Short summary from benefits vendor:
- Carrier A (large national plan): prefers SSN or ITIN for dependent verification; may suspend if no verification within 60 days.
- Carrier B (global plan): accepts passport + marriage cert; can set up coverage while ITIN is pending.
- Dental/Vision: typically limited to US provider lists, international claims are on a case-by-case basis.
We can confirm specific plan behavior if you tell me which plans you want to enroll them in.

Maya: Practical checklist (what to DM/upload):
```
- Clear scan/photo of spouse passport (biographic page)
- Marriage certificate (certified translation if needed)
- If no SSN: ITIN or W-7 receipt (or a note that you will apply)
- Spouse full legal name, DOB, country of residence
- Desired coverages (medical, dental, vision, life)
```

Maya: Payroll/tax note: employee premium share for medical/dental is typically pre-tax; adding a spouse changes your deductions once processed. It does not make your spouse US-taxable just by enrolling them, but if you elect certain employer-provided taxable benefits we’ll coordinate with payroll. If your spouse has income or other US tax considerations, consult tax advisor — People Ops can share how premiums will appear on your payroll stub.

Alex: Thanks — I’ll DM the passport + marriage cert and indicate I want medical + dental. Do I need to apply for an ITIN before submitting?

Carlos: You can submit enrollment first with passport + marriage cert and indicate ITIN is pending. For Carrier A there may be follow-up verification; Carrier B can usually process while ITIN is pending. We’ll flag the enrollment so it doesn’t auto-deny.

Maya: Perfect. Once you DM the docs I’ll start the dependent addition flow and confirm whether we need anything else. Coverage effective date: usually next 1st of the month following processing (depends on when paperwork is completed).

Alex: DMing now — thanks everyone! :thumbsup:

Maya: Got it — reviewing now. If anything missing I’ll @you in this thread.

Carlos: If helpful I can email the carrier rep to pre-check international acceptance. Want me to loop them in?

Alex: Yes please, that would be great.

Maya: Will keep the thread updated.
